hints: The bag contains 4 red and 5 blue marbles (total 9). Head occurs with P(H) = 1/3 and Tail with P(T) = 2/3.
It is easiest to find the complement: P(no red marbles selected).
If Head: 1 marble chosen, so P(no red | H) = P(Blue) = 5/9.
If Tail: 2 marbles chosen without replacement, so P(no red | T) = P(Blue and Blue) = (5/9) * (4/8) = 5/18.
walkthrough:
Calculate the probability of the complementary event, selecting no red marbles (i.e. only blue marbles):
- If Head is thrown ($P(H) = 1/3$): select $1$ marble:
$$P(\text{no red} \mid H) = \frac{5}{9}$$
- If Tail is thrown ($P(T) = 2/3$): select $2$ marbles without replacement:
$$P(\text{no red} \mid T) = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{4}{8} = \frac{20}{72} = \frac{5}{18}$$

Apply the law of total probability to find $P(\text{no red})$:
$$P(\text{no red}) = \left(\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{9}\right) + \left(\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{5}{18}\right) = \frac{5}{27} + \frac{10}{54} = \frac{5}{27} + \frac{5}{27} = \frac{10}{27}$$

Subtract from $1$ to find the probability of at least one red marble:
$$P(\text{at least one red}) = 1 - \frac{10}{27} = \frac{17}{27} \approx 0.630$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Understand the two-stage experiment:
- A biased coin is tossed: $P(H) = \frac{1}{3}$ and $P(T) = 1 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{2}{3}$.
- A bag contains $4$ red marbles and $5$ blue marbles (total $4 + 5 = 9$ marbles).
- If Head: Seva selects $1$ marble at random.
- If Tail: Seva selects $2$ marbles at random without replacement.

Step 2: Use the complement rule:
'At least one red marble' is the complement of 'no red marbles':
$$P(\text{at least one red}) = 1 - P(\text{no red})$$

Step 3: Calculate P(no red) along both branches of the tree diagram:
Branch 1: Coin shows Head ($P(H) = \frac{1}{3}$):
Seva picks $1$ marble from the bag. To get no red, he must pick a blue marble:
$$P(\text{Blue} \mid H) = \frac{5}{9}$$
$$P(H \cap \text{no red}) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{5}{27}$$

Branch 2: Coin shows Tail ($P(T) = \frac{2}{3}$):
Seva picks $2$ marbles without replacement. To get no red, both marbles must be blue:
$$P(B_1 \cap B_2 \mid T) = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{4}{8} = \frac{5}{9} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{18}$$
$$P(T \cap \text{no red}) = \frac{2}{3} \times \frac{5}{18} = \frac{10}{54} = \frac{5}{27}$$

Step 4: Sum the probabilities of the mutually exclusive no-red paths:
$$P(\text{no red}) = \frac{5}{27} + \frac{5}{27} = \frac{10}{27}$$

Step 5: Subtract from 1:
$$P(\text{at least one red}) = 1 - \frac{10}{27} = \frac{17}{27} \approx 0.630$$
(To 3 significant figures).

hints: Use the conditional probability formula: P(Head | no red) = P(Head and no red) / P(no red).
From part (a), P(Head and no red) = (1/3) * (5/9) = 5/27.
From part (a), the denominator P(no red) = 10/27.
walkthrough:
State the conditional probability formula:
$$P(H \mid \text{no red}) = \frac{P(H \cap \text{no red})}{P(\text{no red})}$$

Substitute the joint probability and total probability obtained in part (a):
$$P(H \cap \text{no red}) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{5}{27}$$
$$P(\text{no red}) = \frac{10}{27}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: State the definition of conditional probability:
$$P(H \mid \text{no red}) = \frac{P(H \cap \text{no red})}{P(\text{no red})}$$

Step 2: Identify the numerator:
The probability that the coin landed on Head and no red marble was selected was computed in part (a) as:
$$P(H \cap \text{no red}) = \frac{1}{3} \times \frac{5}{9} = \frac{5}{27}$$

Step 3: Identify the denominator:
The total probability that no red marble was selected was also calculated in part (a):
$$P(\text{no red}) = \frac{10}{27}$$
